samples.question: The picture shows one framed lattice of 7 rows and 12 columns of short straight bars, all the same length, thickness and colour. Each bar leans either to the left or to the right of vertical, always by the same small angle. A dashed coloured line down the middle gap of the lattice, with a triangular pointer above and below the frame, marks the fold axis: it separates the 6 left columns from the 6 right columns. Fold the right half onto the left half about that axis, so that the bar in row r and column 12 lands on the bar in row r and column 1, column 11 lands on column 2, and so on. Almost everywhere the right-hand bar is the exact mirror image of the bar it lands on, meaning the two bars of a pair lean towards each other or away from each other. In the remaining cells the pair breaks that mirror rule: both bars lean the same way, so they look parallel. Mark exactly those broken cells on the left half. The marked cells form one of these five symbols inside a 5-by-5 block of cells, each symbol using exactly 9 cells: plus (a full centre row crossed by a full centre column), ex (the two full diagonals of the block, crossing at its centre), tee (a full top row with a centre column hanging from it), ell (a full left column with a full bottom row), cee (a full left column with a short bar across the top and a short bar across the bottom, open on the right). Which of the five symbols do the marked cells form? Answer with one word.
